exposure: Nulliparous women with a single cephalic term pregnancy, labor induced or delivered by C-section before labor (Group 2)
Women with a single cephalic preterm pregnancy (Group 10)
Multiparous women with a single cephalic term pregnancy and at least one previous C-section (Group 5)
cohort: 8572 women giving birth at a private health facility in Greece
finding: The Robson classification revealed that the largest contributors to the cesarean section rate were nulliparous women with a single cephalic term pregnancy (Group 2), multiparous women with a single cephalic term pregnancy and a previous C-section (Group 5), women with a single cephalic preterm pregnancy (Group 10), and women with multiple pregnancies (Group 8).
mod_finding: The study identified the Robson classification groups with the highest contribution to Cesarean section rates, including nulliparous women with term pregnancies (labor induced or Cesarean before labor), multiparous women with previous Cesarean sections, and women with preterm or multiple pregnancies.
